subject: english
title: Reading comprehension
setup: A small cooperative bank in a hill town noticed that many farmers withdrew all their savings right after the harvest and spent it within weeks. Instead of lecturing them, the bank started a simple scheme: any farmer who left a part of the harvest money untouched for six months received a slightly higher rate of interest and a free visit from an advisor. Within two seasons, deposits grew steadily, and farmers began to plan purchases of seeds and tools in advance rather than borrowing at high rates from local moneylenders. The manager later said that the extra interest mattered less than the visits, because farmers trusted advice given at their own doorstep.

questions.question: Why did the bank start the scheme?
options: To stop farmers from taking loans
Because farmers spent their savings soon after the harvest
To compete with other banks in the town
questions.explanation: The passage says farmers 'withdrew all their savings right after the harvest and spent it within weeks', and the bank responded to that.

questions.question: What did a farmer have to do to get the higher rate?
options: Leave part of the harvest money untouched for six months
Attend a meeting at the bank
questions.explanation: 'any farmer who left a part of the harvest money untouched for six months received a slightly higher rate'.

questions.question: According to the manager, what made the biggest difference?
questions.explanation: 'the extra interest mattered less than the visits'.

questions.question: Which word is closest in meaning to 'steadily' as used in the passage?
questions.explanation: 'Deposits grew steadily' means they grew at a regular, continuous pace.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the moneylenders?
options: They charged more than the bank
They closed down after two seasons
questions.explanation: Farmers stopped 'borrowing at high rates from local moneylenders', which implies the moneylenders were costlier.

subject: english
title: Reading comprehension
setup: When a town library introduced a rule that books could be borrowed without a card, some staff feared that many books would never come back. The librarian decided to test the idea for one year. Borrowers only had to write their name and phone number in a register. To everyone's surprise, the number of missing books hardly changed, while the number of borrowers almost doubled. Many new readers were students and daily-wage workers who had found the card process too slow. The librarian concluded that most people respond to trust with responsibility, and that rules meant to prevent a few losses can keep many honest people away.

questions.question: What was the staff's fear about the new rule?
options: That books would not be returned
That the library would become crowded
That the register would be lost
questions.explanation: 'some staff feared that many books would never come back'.

questions.question: What happened to the number of borrowers?
questions.explanation: 'the number of borrowers almost doubled'.

questions.question: Why had many new readers not borrowed books before?
options: The card process was too slow for them
questions.explanation: They 'had found the card process too slow'.

questions.question: Which of these best states the librarian's conclusion?
options: Trusting people usually makes them act responsibly
questions.explanation: 'most people respond to trust with responsibility'.

questions.question: What is the tone of the passage?
questions.explanation: It describes a trusting experiment that worked better than expected.

subject: english
title: Reading comprehension
setup: Digital payments have made it easy to pay for a cup of tea with a phone, but this convenience has a hidden side. When people pay with cash, they see the money leave their hands, and many feel the cost more sharply. With a quick tap, the sense of spending fades, and small purchases add up without being noticed. Some families now set a weekly limit in their payment app or check their transaction history every Sunday. Such habits do not reject technology; they simply bring back the awareness that cash once gave naturally.

questions.question: What is the 'hidden side' of digital payments, according to the passage?
options: People may spend more without noticing
questions.explanation: 'the sense of spending fades, and small purchases add up without being noticed'.

questions.question: Why do people feel the cost more with cash?
options: They see the money leave their hands
questions.explanation: 'they see the money leave their hands, and many feel the cost more sharply'.

questions.question: What do some families do to control spending?
options: Set a weekly limit or review their transactions
questions.explanation: They 'set a weekly limit in their payment app or check their transaction history every Sunday'.

questions.question: The word 'fades' in the passage most nearly means:
questions.explanation: 'The sense of spending fades' means it becomes weaker.

questions.question: Which title suits the passage best?
options: How to Open a Bank Account
Staying Aware in a Cashless World
questions.explanation: The passage is about keeping spending awareness while paying digitally.

subject: english
title: Reading comprehension
setup: A young engineer joined a company that had used the same paper forms for twenty years. She suggested moving everything to a computer system, but the senior clerks resisted, saying the old way worked fine. Instead of pushing harder, she asked them to list the three tasks they disliked most. All of them named the monthly report, which took two full days to prepare by hand. She built a small tool that produced the report in minutes. After seeing the result, the clerks themselves asked what else could be moved to the computer.

questions.question: How did the senior clerks first react to her suggestion?
options: They reported her to the manager
questions.explanation: 'the senior clerks resisted, saying the old way worked fine'.

questions.question: What did the engineer do instead of pushing harder?
options: She asked the clerks which tasks they disliked most
She changed all forms at once
questions.explanation: 'she asked them to list the three tasks they disliked most'.

questions.question: How long did the monthly report take by hand?
questions.explanation: 'took two full days to prepare by hand'.

questions.question: What changed the clerks' minds?
options: Seeing a disliked task done in minutes
questions.explanation: 'After seeing the result, the clerks themselves asked what else could be moved'.

questions.question: What lesson does the passage suggest?
options: Change is easier when it solves people's own problems
Engineers should not work with clerks
questions.explanation: She won support by fixing the task the clerks themselves disliked.

subject: english
title: Reading comprehension
setup: In many villages, women's self-help groups meet once a week to save small amounts together. Each member puts in a fixed sum, and the group lends from this common fund to members who need money for a sewing machine, a cow or school fees. Because the borrowers are neighbours who meet every week, repayment rates are often very high. Banks have noticed this and now lend to such groups as a whole. The weekly meeting does more than move money: members say it gives them confidence to speak in public and to deal with officials.

questions.question: How often do the groups meet?
questions.explanation: 'meet once a week'.

questions.question: Why are repayment rates often high?
options: Borrowers are neighbours who meet every week
questions.explanation: 'Because the borrowers are neighbours who meet every week, repayment rates are often very high'.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT given as a use of loans?
questions.explanation: The passage lists a sewing machine, a cow and school fees; land is not mentioned.

questions.question: What have banks started doing?
options: Lending to the groups as a whole
questions.explanation: 'Banks ... now lend to such groups as a whole'.

questions.question: What benefit beyond money do members mention?
options: Confidence to speak in public and deal with officials
questions.explanation: 'it gives them confidence to speak in public and to deal with officials'.
